title: Vikings Were Cleaner Than the English
hook: English monks complained that Norse raiders bathed every Saturday.

scenes.text: Pop culture portrays Vikings as filthy savages covered in mud and grime, but historical records prove the exact opposite.

scenes.text: Archaeologists discover personal grooming kits in almost every Viking grave: carved bone hair combs, bronze tweezers, and ear spoons.

scenes.voicedText: Archaeologists discover personal grooming kits in almost every Viking grave: carved bone hair combs, bronze tweezers, and ear spoons.

scenes.text: While Anglo-Saxon peasants rarely washed, Vikings had a mandatory weekly bath day every Saturday called 'Laugardagur'—literally 'Washing Day'.

scenes.voicedText: While Anglo-Saxon peasants rarely washed, Vikings had a mandatory weekly bath day every Saturday called 'Laugardagur'—literally 'Washing Day'.

scenes.text: Norse men even bleached their hair and beards golden-blonde using strong lye soap, which also repelled lice and fleas.
